candidates.change_summary: Change the unlockTime condition from < block.timestamp to <= block.timestamp in the require guard.
Change the amount condition from > 0 to >= 0 in the require guard.
Change the asset equality condition to inequality in the require guard.
Delete the delete statement that clears the pending flash decision entry.
Replace the delete statement with a no-op self-assignment so the mapping entry is not cleared.
Replace the flash-decision pending-condition require with a check that reverses the unlockTime comparison, so a pending decision can only withdraw before unlock instead of after.
Replace the asset-match comparison with a check that the pending asset is a different token, changing which withdrawals are accepted.
Replace the pending-amount positivity check with a zero-or-more check, allowing zero-value withdrawals.
Delete the final state-clearing statement that removes the pending flash-governance decision after withdrawal.
Replace the token transfer recipient with the target contract address, sending the withdrawn amount to the wrong account.
The endConfiguration function body now sets configured to false instead of true, so after the call the public configured() value differs.
The assignment statement in endConfiguration is deleted, so the function no longer updates configured and it retains its prior value.
Change the access-control condition so setDAO only rejects when DAO is already set and the caller is neither DAO nor unconfigured.
Remove the access-control require statement from setDAO entirely, allowing any caller to overwrite DAO at any time.
Replace the DAO assignment so setDAO writes address(0) into DAO instead of the provided dao argument.
